solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Challenge wins always

parts.note: wins as a verb means gains
ay (or aye) is an old word for always, as in 'for ay'

explanation.surface: A sports report: a challenger keeps on winning.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay a claim is to contradict or dispute it, so it is a synonym of challenge as a verb.

clue.text: On island forage for goat

parts.note: Capri is the island in the Bay of Naples
corn is grain fed to livestock, so forage or fodder

explanation.surface: A goat on an island goes looking for food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forage' reads as a verb, but it is a noun here: animal feed, CORN.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricorn is the zodiac sign whose emblem is the goat, so the sign stands for it.

clue.text: A card is free from anxiety

parts.note: to card wool is to comb it out, which is also to tease it

explanation.surface: Someone who is a card, a joker, is relaxed and carefree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card' looks like a noun (a joker, a playing card) but is the verb for combing out wool, TEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being relaxed and untroubled is an idiomatic sense of the phrase, a synonym for calm.

clue.text: Hinting I have to follow everything American …

indicators.note: the words for 'I have' are told to follow, to come after, the other pieces

parts.note: everything means all
US is short for American, as in United States
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: A speaker hints that they will go along with everything American.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs the clue on into 8 across; it does no work in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusive remarks refer to something indirectly, which is to suggest or imply it.

clue.text: Muck around cage — tidy that; dog's agitated

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up and shaken about, so the letters of these words are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: An owner tells someone to tidy the cage while the dog is getting worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'dog's' is 'is', a link joining the fodder to 'agitated'.
explanation.definitionFit: To act the giddy goat is a British idiom for fooling about, playing the clown.

clue.text: Dress coils and bun for babes?

indicators.note: to dress is to arrange or put in order, so the letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A hairdressing tip: coil and pin your hair in a bun for a baby-faced look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' reads as hairdressing; it signals rearranging. The question mark flags that 'babes' are young animals, not infants.
explanation.definitionFit: Young lions are their babies, so 'babes' is a playful description by example.

clue.text: Item in news is alarmist — fibre's needed

indicators.note: an item contained in the run of words, so the letters sit inside the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A news story is scaremongering, and the diet needs more fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a stiff plant fibre from an agave, used for rope and matting, so it is an example.

clue.text: I must look up for this or I become green first

definitions.text: I must look up for this

indicators.note: first places the colour word before the rest of the pieces

parts.note: vert is the heraldic word for green
go means become, as in 'go red'

explanation.surface: Someone afraid of heights says they must look up, or they will turn green.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is quirky: a sufferer avoids looking down, so must look up.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo is dizziness on looking down from a height, so a sufferer keeps their eyes raised.

clue.text: … graduate to Southern alternative rock

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
alt is short for alternative

explanation.surface: Continuing 4 across: a graduate turns to Southern alternative rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative rock' suggests the music genre; rock is the stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Basalt is a dark volcanic stone, so it is an example of the general term.

clue.text: Itinerant actors exchange pence for shillings to get clothes

indicators.note: exchange one thing for another means swap the first out and put the second in its place

parts.note: troupers are members of a touring theatre company
s is the abbreviation for shillings, the old British coin

explanation.surface: Touring players swap their small change for old coins to buy clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'for' says which coin goes in: pence out, shillings in. A shilling was an old British coin, abbreviated s.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousers are a garment, so an example of the broader word for things worn.

clue.text: Not imagined but could be damn true

indicators.note: these letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A surprised exclamation: you never dreamed it, but it might really be true.
explanation.definitionFit: Undreamt means never dreamt of, so beyond what anyone had pictured or conceived.

clue.text: Caught, unfortunately, after one's infiltrated end of tunnel

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: infiltrated means got inside, so the numeral goes into the regretful word

parts.note: alas is an expression of regret, meaning unfortunately
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone who slipped through is unluckily caught at the far end of the tunnel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is 'one has'. The tunnel is the Channel Tunnel between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Channel Tunnel's French terminal is near this port, so the French end is named by the town.

clue.text: Foreign aristocrat walks to Spain

parts.note: marches means walks, briskly and in step
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A foreign nobleman walks all the way to Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A marchese is an Italian marquis, a nobleman ranking below a duke.

clue.text: Break promise of support to intercept hired thug

indicators.note: intercept means to get in the way of, so the support word sits inside the thug word

parts.note: a goon is a heavy hired to intimidate
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: A backer breaks their pledge to stop a hired heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: To renege on a pledge is the idiomatic sense, as when a politician fails to keep their word.

clue.text: Guide of eight announced search for crest

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the steersman's title is said rather than written

parts.note: the cox steers a rowing eight
to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

explanation.surface: A rowing coxswain's search for a crest or peak.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'eight' is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen, which the cox steers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel's red fleshy comb is its crest, the ridge on top of its head.

clue.text: Curve of yellow bird holding note

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the bird encloses the note

parts.note: the canary is the classic yellow songbird
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A curve traced by a yellow bird as it holds a note in song.
explanation.definitionFit: A catenary is the shape a hanging chain or cable makes, a mathematical arc.

clue.text: European to cross Iowa road

parts.note: to span a river is to cross it
IA is the postal abbreviation for Iowa

explanation.surface: A European sets out to cross an Iowa road.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spaniard comes from Spain, so is a person of that continent by example.

clue.text: A variety act

parts.note: a, as in 'ten pounds a head', means per
a form is a variety or kind

explanation.surface: A short phrase for a music-hall turn: a variety act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety act' suggests music hall; 'variety' is FORM and 'act' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To act on stage is to play a role, so the verb is a synonym of acting.

clue.text: A quote comes back about self-catering — one abstains

indicators.note: about means around, so these pieces enclose the holiday abbreviation
comes back means returns, so the quoting word runs backwards

parts.note: to quote is to cite
SC is the abbreviation for self-catering in holiday listings

explanation.surface: A quote for a self-catering holiday comes back, and one person declines.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic is someone who practises severe self-denial, refusing comforts.

clue.text: Journalist, upset, mischievously spikes sealing of alliance, French-style

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so in this across entry the editor's letters run backwards

parts.note: ED, an editor, is a journalist

indicators.note: doing something mischievously scrambles it, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: An upset reporter mischievously kills the story of an alliance being sealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ED into DE; 'spikes' is a journalist's word for killing a story, but here it is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A French kiss is a passionate open-mouthed one, and a kiss can seal a relationship.

clue.text: Cable, perhaps, sent after start of engagement, express

indicators.note: sent after means placed following, so the politician's name comes behind the opening letter
the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Vince Cable is a British Liberal Democrat politician, an example of a Vince

explanation.surface: A cable telegram dispatched once the engagement starts, to express congratulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cable' looks like a telegram; it is Vince Cable, a former UK cabinet minister.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince a feeling is to show or reveal it, a synonym of the verb express.

clue.text: Mysterious Arab punishment

parts.note: Ar is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic
the cane is a corporal punishment

explanation.surface: A puzzling Arab punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcane means known only to a few, secret or obscure, hence enigmatic.

clue.text: Practised for record time that's given commercial support

indicators.note: support places the advert as a prop beside the record and time pieces

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A record track that gets commercial backing.
explanation.definitionFit: An adept is highly skilled, much practised, an expert.

clue.text: Bugs could make legs itch

indicators.note: could make means the letters might be rearranged into the answer

explanation.surface: Insects might make your legs itch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bugs' reads as insects, the itch-makers; it means faults.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugs in software are faults or errors, minor malfunctions.

clue.text: Examiner not right keeping speed within bounds

indicators.note: not means without, so the abbreviation is removed

parts.note: a moderator checks examination marking

explanation.surface: An examiner who is not right keeps the speed limit.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderato is the musical tempo marking for a moderate pace.

clue.text: Kitchen apprentice promises to cut temperature

indicators.note: cut means remove, so the abbreviation is taken out

parts.note: commits means pledges or promises

explanation.surface: A kitchen trainee promises to turn the heat down.
explanation.definitionFit: A commis is a junior chef working under a station chef in a restaurant.

clue.text: Chopped thyme eaten by a holy man transformed into stone

indicators.note: eaten by means swallowed inside, so the jumbled herb goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: St, saint, is a holy man

indicators.note: chopped means cut up, so the herb's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A saint eats chopped thyme and is miraculously turned to stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Amethyst is a purple quartz gem, an example of a precious stone.
